newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Three S.Korean refiners cut petrol prices again.
newsitem.headline: Three S.Korean refiners cut petrol prices again.

text.p: South Korea's Yukong Ltd, LG-Caltex Oil Corp and Hyundai Oil Refinery Co have reduced retail petrol prices at their pumps for the second time this month to remain competitive against two other refiners, industry sources said on Thursday.
Hyundai lowered its retail petrol price to 832 won a litre on late Wednesday from 842 won announced on Tuesday, Yukong to 837 won from 843 won and LG-Caltex to 839-840 won from 843 won.
The prices were initially cut on April 1 from an average of 845-846 won last month.
Ssangyong Oil Refining Co and Hanwha Energy Co Ltd posted the lowest prices among the refiners on April 1, by setting their prices at 832 won and 831 won respectively.
"In order to keep our market share, we had no choice but to follow Ssangyong and Hanwha's move and additionally cut our petrol prices," said a Hyundai Oil official.
Despite their uniform move to reduce petrol prices, oil refiners said they were concerned about deteriorating profits.
"Price cuts will hurt our profits already hit by the Korean won's depreciation against the dollar," said the Hyundai official.
The won has fallen six percent so far this year.

Industry sources said this was the first time the refiners had engaged in major price cuts since domestic prices of gasoline, kerosene, diesel and C-type fuel oil were deregulated on January 1 and no longer subject to a government-set monthly price ceiling. There was a small price cut in March.

At the end of 1996, Yukong had the largest petrol market share of 38.6 percent, followed by LG-Caltex's 31.4 percent, Ssangyong's 12.1 percent, Hanwha's 10.3 percent and Hyundai's 7.6 percent, official figures showed.
